transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-08 14:00 PDT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (LuminaDocs Head of Search), Marco Ruiz (Eng Lead), Lena Kovacs (Security)

00:00 - Evan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — i'm evan park, i'm the AE on this account, with maya our solutions engineer. how's everybody doing?
00:08 - Priya (LuminaDocs): good, thanks. excited to see the embeddings + rerank flow, we've been trying to lift search relevance across docs.
00:14 - Maya (Redwood SE): awesome, i'll run the demo end-to-end, show the hosted embeddings endpoint, nearest neighbor search, and then our rerank endpoint which re-scores the top-k. we'll also cover console, observability and some optimize suggestions for cost.
00:28 - Marco (LuminaDocs): quick context — we run Elastic for primary search, we also use a vector store for semantic fallback (self-hosted). main pain is results drift and cost when we embed everything.
00:36 - Lena (LuminaDocs): and security is a blocker — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS, and data residency requirements for EMEA.
00:44 - Evan: totally, we'll point out the hosted SLA options and our Private/Dedicated notes but today focus on hosted API.
01:02 - Maya: alright jumping in — here's a simple request to /v1/embeddings, we send your document chunks, get back 1536-d vectors (note: model choice matters, we have curated defaults). example code in the SDK.
01:20 - Maya: transcription note: sometimes the auto-transcripts read "K V cash" instead of KV cache — ignore that, sorry.
01:28 - Marco: are the dims fixed? we have different models in dev vs prod.
01:34 - Maya: yes dims depend on model, but our rerank endpoint accepts vectors + candidate ids; you can send embeddings from any model as long as dims match — if not we'll do a compatibility check and suggest quantized variant.
01:50 - Priya: show us the rerank please — how much lift should we expect?
02:00 - Maya: demo time — here I run a sample query "export compliance summary". First we call the embeddings search (ANN) in about 60ms, we get top 50 candidates. Then we call the rerank model (small reranker) which recomputes a relevance score on each candidate and we return top 5 ordered by rerank score.
02:20 - Maya: note on latency: typical NN search is super fast, rerank cost scales with k and model size — you can do a 2-stage strategy: small k + cheap reranker, or larger k with a stronger model.
02:36 - Priya: what's the per-query cost if we do top50 + rerank small model?
02:42 - Evan: rough ballpark, embeddings call plus ANN cost is low per query, reranker adds model inference cost — we'll send exact pricing but expect a multiplier. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to reduce unit cost.
03:00 - Marco: can we cache embeddings for doc corpus? we don't want to re-embed everything each time.
03:06 - Maya: yes, prefix/KV caching is supported; Redwood does automatic caching for document embeddings and we expose TTLs. also the Console shows token-level cost and cache hit rate.
03:22 - Lena: security — where are the embeddings stored? are they encrypted at rest?
03:30 - Maya: hosted mode stores embeddings encrypted at rest, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated/Private and for hosted we support KMS integrations for enterprise tiers. Audit logs and per-request metadata are in the Console.
03:48 - Priya: data residency — can we ensure EMEA only?
03:54 - Evan: yes, routing by region is supported; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private, but hosted can pin region for your account. we'll include the region options in the security pack we send.
04:12 - Marco: demo question — when we rerank, do we send the original doc text back to the model or only embeddings?
04:18 - Maya: good question — our reranker accepts either embeddings-only (cosine + learned model on embeddings) or text + candidate context for cross-encoder style rerank. Text + context gives best quality but higher token cost.
04:33 - Priya: examples?
04:36 - Maya: i'll show both quickly — first embeddings-only rerank: we compute vector similarity and then a small MLP that takes vector pairs, fast. then cross-encoder rerank: we concat query+candidate snippets and run through a cross-encoder model for final score — it's slower but often yields 5-20% relevance lift depending on dataset.
04:58 - [00:05:00] Maya: demo slide shows sample metrics: recall@10 improves, business metrics like click-through increase. these are sample numbers, your variance depends on data.
05:18 - Marco: do you have a hosted vector index like Pinecone or do you integrate with their stores?
05:24 - Maya: Redwood provides hosted ANN and you can also use external vector stores — we integrate with common ones (Pinecone, Weaviate, self-managed OpenSearch). if you bring your own store, we do routing and rerank on our side.
05:40 - Priya: what's the onboarding like? can we trial with a subset of docs?
05:44 - Evan: yes, short trial project, we can give API keys scoped to a project, and a short POC. we'll also run a quick benchmark for your dataset.
05:56 - Lena: on compliance, we need SOC2 type II evidence and proof of key separation.
06:02 - Maya: we have SOC2 docs and a published whitepaper on key management; i'll attach excerpts. for hosted we offer envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private you get customer-controlled KMS.
06:18 - Priya: what about RBAC and SSO?
06:22 - Evan: SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported; RBAC with role templates. Console has audit trails per token.
06:30 - [00:06:45] Marco: technical — for high throughput we have bursty traffic, will the hosted API autoscale?
06:36 - Maya: hosted auto-scales to reasonable limits; for predictable high throughput we recommend Dedicated. but we do support burst capacity and throttling policies per account.
06:48 - Priya: any gotchas around embedding dimension/quantization?
06:52 - Maya: quantization affects accuracy; we recommend evaluating a quantized model in sandbox — Redwood Optimize can simulate unit cost and expected quality delta for quantization profiles.
07:06 - Evan: quick note — i'll share an Optimize report template that maps cost vs latency vs quality.
07:12 - [00:07:20] Maya: switching to Console — here's the project page, you can see token usage, per-route latency heatmaps, rerank ops per minute, and top prompts. the debug traces help identify tail latency.
07:34 - Marco: can we get per-customer tracing to tie back to our request IDs?
07:38 - Maya: yes you can pass x-request-id and we surface it in traces. we also export to your tracing system via hooks.
07:46 - Priya: curious — how do you handle versioning/rollouts for rerank models?
07:50 - Maya: model rollouts can be canaryed, A/B tested with automatic fallback policies. Console shows per-model metrics.
08:02 - Marco: what kind of latency numbers for reranker?
08:06 - Maya: depends on model size — small reranker 20-80ms per document, cross-encoder can be 150-600ms depending on token lengths. you can parallelize rerank across GPUs in Dedicated.
08:26 - Priya: okay show us the real demo with our sample text — we shared a tiny dataset in the worksheet.
08:32 - Maya: loading... (typing) okay i've loaded the sample dataset you uploaded — i'll run a query and show raw NN results then rerank.
08:46 - [00:09:00] Maya: querying "data retention policy for european customers" — got top 50, look at candidate 1 it's somewhat on-topic but missing context, candidate 3 is actually better after rerank. rerank bumped candidate 3 to top because the cross-encoder picked up phrase matches in the paragraph.
09:12 - Marco: wow that actually seems closer. can you show the request/response?
09:18 - Maya: sure — here's a sanitized request: POST /v1/rerank { query: "...", candidates: [{id: "doc_123", embedding: [...]} , ...] } response includes scores and normalized confidence.
09:36 - Priya: transcription glitch: i see sometimes the speaker labels switch; it's fine.
09:40 - Evan: yes Fireflies sometimes mislabels, ignore the speaker flicker.
09:46 - Maya: another feature — you can pass business rules to rerank (bump if doc metadata matches). useful for boosting SLA pages.
10:00 - Marco: about metrics — how do we measure lift vs baseline?
10:04 - Maya: we'll run A/B in production or offline evals; Console has prompt/eval suites to track regressions. also you can upload labeled pairs for supervised evals.
10:20 - Lena: security follow-up: can we redact PII before sending to Redwood?
10:24 - Maya: yes you can run a local redaction step or use our in-pipeline redaction rule; we can also set a policy to avoid storing raw text for certain projects.
10:36 - Priya: licensing and IP — do you retain rights?
10:40 - Evan: standard SaaS terms, we don't claim customer IP. we'll include summary in the security pack.
10:46 - [00:11:00] Marco: performance test idea — can you run a benchmark: our crawl (100k docs) against a 10qps sustained workload?
11:06 - Maya: yes we do benchmark runs; for hosted we'd simulate and show expected latency/cost; for Dedicated we'll provide sizing guidance.
11:18 - Priya: timeline — if we like results can we start POC next week?
11:22 - Evan: yes, tentative POC start next week, 2 week pilot. we'll follow up with onboarding checklist.
11:30 - Lena: also need contractual info — DPAs, data processing addendum.
11:34 - Evan: yep we'll include those.
11:40 - [00:11:50] Maya: i want to show a quick Optimize workflow — it analyzes your query distribution, suggests batching, quant profiles, and a recommended rerank config to hit your latency target under a cost budget.
11:58 - Priya: can Optimize link suggestions to Console metrics automatically?
12:02 - Maya: yes Optimize can push suggested configs and you can apply them from Console or via API.
12:12 - Marco: any limits on candidate k? and cost if we increase k to 200?
12:16 - Maya: technical limit is large (thousands) but cost and latency scale. we'll advise best k based on recall curves we can compute during POC.
12:28 - Priya: okay sounds good. can you email the sample rerank config?
12:32 - Evan: yes, i'll send a starter config with recommended models and k.
12:38 - [00:13:10] Lena: one more security nit — can we get a list of sub-processors?
13:16 - Maya: yes, we'll include the standard sub-processor list in the security pack.
13:22 - Evan: to recap — we'll send pricing & tier comparison, security pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS notes), create a trial project and scoped API keys, and schedule POC check-in.
13:36 - Priya: thanks, that aligns with our asks.
13:40 - Marco: quick question from infra — do you expose prometheus metrics?
13:44 - Maya: yes we can export metrics to Prometheus/Grafana or push to your cloud monitoring.
13:50 - Priya: timeline/next step — target start 2027-05-10 for trial?
13:54 - Evan: we'll aim to have keys and docs by 2027-05-11, pricing by 2027-05-10.
14:04 - [00:14:20] Maya: any final questions?
14:08 - Priya: none, thanks.
14:10 - Marco: none from me.
14:12 - Lena: looking forward to security docs.
14:14 - Evan: great thanks all. we'll follow up in an email with artifacts: pricing sheet, security pack, rerank starter config, and onboarding checklist.
14:24 - Meeting ended.
